flagged.evidence: The proof says, “patch them by a partition which is constant in the normal directions near each sheet, preserving the product germs,” then claims the normal exponential map identifies the collars exactly with the model sheets. The cited tubular-neighbourhood theorem supplies only a diffeomorphism from an open normal-bundle neighbourhood to an ambient neighbourhood; the product-chart lemma supplies charts near a point; and the partition-of-unity theorem supplies an ordinary subordinate partition. None establishes the required simultaneous adapted metric, special partition, or framed tube. The germ-isomorphism result only compares tubes after they exist. This is the central prerequisite for the model, not an immediate omitted coordinate detail.

The title claims uniqueness for tubes on the same normal bundle. But the cited definition requires only an open normal-bundle neighbourhood and an embedding with Φ(0_p)=i(p); it does not require matching vertical derivatives. The Statement itself adds that dΦ₁ and dΦ₂ must induce the same normal-quotient map and warns that fixing the zero section alone is insufficient. For S={0}⊂R, Φ₁(v)=v and Φ₂(v)=−v are both tubes under the definition, but no isotopy of tube maps fixing S can join them: the derivative at 0 would have to vary continuously from +1 to −1 while remaining nonzero.

The page says “tubular neighbourhoods of the same normal bundle are unique up to ambient isotopy” without the compatibility of their induced vertical normal maps. The current corollary requires those maps to agree, and the repository definition of a tubular neighbourhood requires only Φ(0_p)=i(p). The tubes v↦v and v↦−v for a point in R satisfy that definition but cannot be joined by an isotopy fixing the point, since the derivative sign cannot change through nonzero derivatives.

The title states the conclusion for isotopic embeddings without a compact-source or other extension-control hypothesis. The repository definition says compactness is not part of the definition of isotopy. The current Statement assumes M compact, and the current noncompact-line remark gives a properly embedded trefoil-knotted line smoothly isotopic through embeddings to the straight line while their complements have nonisomorphic fundamental groups (the trefoil group versus Z). Thus the title asserts more than the stated result supports.
